questions.stem_latex:
When Fred was born, his parents opened a new savings account and made a deposit of \$300. At the start of each subsequent six-month period, his parents make a deposit of \$300. The account earns an interest rate of 6% per annum, compounded half-yearly.

Let $A_n$ be the amount (in dollars) in the account at the end of $n^{th}$ half-year.

parts.label: c
parts.latex: Show that the amount available for withdrawal at the end of the 18$^{\text{th}}$ year will be \$19552 to the nearest dollar. (Assume that no withdrawals are made from the fund during this time.)

parts.label: a
parts.latex: Calculate the Pearson's correlation coefficient. Give your answer correct to 3 decimal places.

parts.label: b
parts.latex: Find the equation of the least-squares line of best fit, expressing the height ($h$) in terms of years ($t$). Give your answer correct to 2 decimal places.

parts.label: c
parts.latex: Use the equation of the least-squares line of best fit to predict the giraffe's height in the fifth year. Give your answer correct to 1 decimal place.

parts.label: d
parts.latex:
Estimate how many years it will take for the giraffe to reach a height of 6.1 metres.

Give your answer correct to 1 decimal place.

questions.stem_latex: An object that was initially at the origin moves with velocity ($v$ m/s) given by $v=24+10t-t^2$.

parts.label: a
parts.latex: Find the maximum speed of the object.

parts.label: b
parts.latex: Find the acceleration when the object is at rest.

parts.label: c
parts.latex: Find the total distance travelled by the object during the first 15 seconds.

questions.stem_latex:
Arjun borrows \$1,000,000 for a period of 10 years at an interest rate of 0.5% per month, compounded monthly. At the end of each month, a repayment of \$$M$ is made.

Let \$$A_n$ be the amount owing after the $n^{th}$ repayment has been made.

parts.label: c
parts.latex: Hence show that the monthly instalment $M$ is given by: $M=\dfrac{5000(1.005)^{120}}{1.005^{120}-1}$.

parts.label: d
parts.latex: Find the amount still owing to the bank after 5 years, correct to two decimal places.

questions.stem_latex: The acceleration ($a$ m/s$^2$) of an object at time $t$ seconds is given by $a=\dfrac{-1}{(5t+1)^2}$. The object is initially 3 metres to the left of the origin travelling with velocity 1 m/s.

parts.label: a
parts.latex: Find an expression for the object's velocity ($v$) at time $t$.

parts.label: b
parts.latex: Find the limiting speed of the object.

parts.label: c
parts.latex: Find the position of the object at the end of the 10$^{\text{th}}$ second. (Answer to the nearest metre)

solutions.latex:
$n=35$, so the median is the 18th score: median $=11$.

Lower quartile = median of the lower 17 scores = 9th score $=11$. Upper quartile = 27th score $=12$.

Mean $=\dfrac{10\times6+11\times18+12\times6+13\times5}{35}=\dfrac{395}{35}\approx11.29$.

The median and lower quartile are equal. Answer: (C)
The points fall steadily from left to right and lie close to a straight line, so the correlation is strong and negative. Answer: (A)

At $A$ the graph is decreasing, so $v=\dfrac{dx}{dt}<0$.

The graph is concave up at $A$, so $a=\dfrac{d^2x}{dt^2}>0$. Answer: (A)

Displacement increases while $v>0$ and decreases while $v<0$.

$v<0$ for $0<t<1$, $v>0$ for $1<t<3$ and $v<0$ for $3<t<4$. The area above the axis from $t=1$ to $t=3$ is larger than the area below from $t=0$ to $t=1$, so the displacement is greatest at $t=3$. Answer: (C)

Since $2e^t>0$ and $4e^{-t}>0$ for all values of $t$, then $2e^t+4e^{-t}>0$ for all values of $t$.

$\therefore$ the particle will never be at rest.

2: obtain all three $Q_1$, $Q_2$, $Q_3$ correctly; 1: obtain any two $Q$'s correctly, or obtain correct positions
2: box-plot above axis with correct extremes; 1: plotted box or extremes
2: correct solution; 1: write an expression for $A_n$, or uses sum of a GP formula without establishing $A_n$

$v=-t^2+10t+24$

The maximum speed is at the turning point.

$$\begin{aligned}t&=-\dfrac{b}{2a} \\ &=-\dfrac{10}{2\times(-1)} \\ &=5\end{aligned}$$

$$\begin{aligned}v_{\max}&=24\times10\times5-5^2 \\ &=49\text{ m/s}\end{aligned}$$
review_reasons: marking guideline answers maximum velocity (49 m/s at t = 5); speed |v| is unbounded for t > 12, so 'maximum speed' is only 49 m/s if the domain is limited (e.g. 0 <= t <= 12)
guideline line '24 x 10 x 5 - 5^2' transcribed as printed (should be 24 + 10 x 5 - 5^2)

solutions.latex:
The object is at rest when $v=0$

$$\begin{aligned}-t^2+10t+24&=0 \\ t^2-10t-24&=0 \\ (t-12)(t+2)&=0\end{aligned}$$

$t=12$ ($t\ge0$)

$$\begin{aligned}a&=\dfrac{dv}{dt} \\ &=-2t+10 \\ &=-2\times12+10 \\ &=-14\text{ m/s}^2\end{aligned}$$
solutions.marks_breakdown: 3: correct solution; 2: obtain $t=12$ and $a=-2t+10$; 1: obtain $-t^2+10t+24=0$ or $t=12$

solutions.latex:
$$\begin{aligned}x&=\int v\,dt \\ &=\int(-t^2+10t+24)\,dt \\ &=-\dfrac{t^3}{3}+5t^2+24t+C\end{aligned}$$

$t=0$, $x=0$: $0=0+0+0+C$, $\therefore C=0$

$$x=-\dfrac{t^3}{3}+5t^2+24t$$

$t=0$, $x=0$

$t=12$, $x=-\dfrac{12^3}{3}+5\times12^2+24\times12=432$ (the object is at rest at $t=12$ in (b))

$t=15$, $x=-\dfrac{15^3}{3}+5\times15^2+24\times15=360$

$$\begin{aligned}\text{Distance travelled}&=432+(432-360) \\ &=504\text{ m}\end{aligned}$$
solutions.marks_breakdown: 3: correct solution; 2: correct displacement at $t=12$ and at $t=15$; 1: correct displacement at $t=15$ or $t=12$
2: correct solution; 1: substantially progress to obtain correct solution, or obtain $A_n$ with GP

solutions.latex:
$v=\dfrac{1}{5(5t+1)}+0.8$

As $t\to\infty$, $\dfrac{1}{5(5t+1)}\to0$

$v\to0.8$

Limiting speed of the object is $0.8$ m/s

$v=\dfrac{1}{5(5t+1)}+0.8$

$$\begin{aligned}x&=\int v\,dt \\ &=\int\left(\dfrac{1}{5(5t+1)}+0.8\right)dt \\ &=\dfrac{1}{5}\times\dfrac{\log_e(5t+1)}{5}+0.8t+C \\ &=\dfrac{\log_e(5t+1)}{25}+0.8t+C\end{aligned}$$

When $t=0$, $x=-3$:

$$\begin{aligned}-3&=\dfrac{\log_e(5\times0+1)}{25}+0.8\times0+C \\ \therefore C&=-3\end{aligned}$$

$$x=\dfrac{1}{25}\log_e(5t+1)+0.8t-3$$

When $t=10$:

$$\begin{aligned}x&=\dfrac{1}{25}\log_e(5\times10+1)+0.8\times10-3 \\ &=5.157\text{ m}\end{aligned}$$

$\approx5$ m to the right of the origin
